answer: Coordination Tariff Ledger. Each agent pays per pairwise interaction, and the tariff for an island of N linked identities scales with the count of distinct counterparties, so a sybil cluster pays to wire its interior. The ledger folds every settlement through a cipher of the payer's prior coordination graph, charging repeated dense cooperation more than sparse contact. Attackers face umber-scaled surcharges as overlapping identities accumulate, making each additional fake identity costlier than the last.
